summary: RAG anti-modal self-contrast: greedy anchor then surpass
hypothesis: Showing the model its own greedy (most-generic) output as a negative anchor and asking it to generate a fresher, sharper set should push coverage past the modal cluster — because a maximally self-relevant contrast should be a stronger signal than a fixed neutral anchor (exp011) or raw temperature (exp024).
technique: A two-stage RAG pipeline: stage 1 retrieves exemplars and generates a greedy draft (most-confident = most-generic modal output); stage 2 receives that draft back as a dynamic negative anchor and makes a fresh generation call instructed to surpass it — avoiding any select/critique judgment step that failed in earlier experiments.
